A brief summary of the control scheme is as follows: • Occupied time = 6:00am – 6:00pm Off-peak time = 6:00am – 4:00pm, space conditioning from base HP o On-peak time = 4:00pm – 6:00pm, space conditioning from TES if available, o otherwise from base HP • Unoccupied time: 6:00pm – 6:00am On-peak time = 6:00pm – 9:00pm, space conditioning from base HP only; o thermostat temperature setback to minimize space conditioning energy requirements; space Off-peak time = 9:00pm – 6:00am, TES recharging whenever the o thermostat has no space conditioning call; space conditioning from base HP only; thermostat temperature setback to minimize space conditioning energy and increase likelihood of TES recharge Page 93 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park Figure 91: HP-TES system controller decision tree The low-level control will modulate the reversing valves and expansion valves to enable proper operation. This also includes controlling the degree of subcooling using the outdoor EXV alone rather than two EXVs at the brazed PHX and outdoor HX (Figure 92). The PID parameters were updated in the four corresponding modes that benefit from this simplification: baseline HP heating, HP-TES heating recharge, HP-TES heating discharge, and HP-TES cooling discharge. After installation, numerous challenges were identified with the supervisory controller, primarily due to improper reading of the thermostat call, resulting in continuous operation of the unit in a fixed mode without TES. The team worked to develop a second supervisory controller, along with multiple software updates pushed via internet connection, to address these issues. However, challenges with the supervisory controller persisted, and the field unit could not run in TES mode as intended. While the control challenges were not addressed before project completion, the comprehensive laboratory testing indicated strong potential for the technology. Moreover, the lessons learned during controller development can be leveraged in future work toward successfully field implementation of this proposed technology. HP-TES Field Test: Expected Peak Demand Reduction While the HP-TES field controller did not operate as required, base HP operation was conducted and data recorded during Summer 2025, in Rancho Cucamonga, CA. Using the validated HP-TES complete transient model from Milestone 2.2, base HP validations were conducted, primarily focusing on power demand throughout a selected summer day (July 2nd 2025). The transient model was simulated in base HP mode only, with all check valves surrounding the plate heat exchanger closed. Results show excellent agreement throughout the day in power demand, providing confidence in utilizing the experimentally validated models for estimating the actual expected performance at the field location.
